tara: Repro: our Kotlin sample app sometimes sends duplicate POST /purchase after 401 + Authenticator refresh. Not a loop but two side-effects.

ben: Client stack? Retrofit/OkHttp versions?

tara: Retrofit 2.9 + OkHttp 4.11 wrapped by our SDK. Authenticator does blocking refresh and returns response.request.newBuilder().header("Authorization", token).build().

kai: Quick thoughts: FormBody is replayable so OkHttp can resend on a new connection. Also proxies or HTTP/2 can cause original to be forwarded late.

ben: Can you share minimal log snippet?

tara: Logs: 
``
CLIENT: POST /purchase id=aa conn=3
SERVER: 401 id=aa
AUTH: refreshing token
CLIENT: replay POST /purchase id=aa conn=7
SERVER: 200 id=aa
SERVER: also got original POST id=aa (delayed)
```

kai: If switching to a non-buffered RequestBody removes dupes, that's telling. Options: mark bodies non-repeatable for mutating calls, add idempotency-key header, or change SDK retry policy to avoid replay after Authenticator paths.

ben: Also validate whether our coroutine CallAdapter could be rerunning calls after auth races. Try plain Call.enqueue() in a tiny repro.

ci-bot: Snapshot redwood-sdk 0.14.3 with okhttp 4.12 available for testing.

tara: I will: 1) try non-buffered body experiment, 2) test snapshot, 3) add idempotency in sample. Will open repro in repo and ping. Thanks. :thumbsup:
